The third of these shared tables, and the starkest divergence of the three:
the simulator was not mirroring the engine at all here. Its edge filter read
only the source handle and never the edge's condition, so an edge marked
'error' was followed after the node SUCCEEDED. A user marks a cleanup branch
as the error path in the EdgeConditionPanel, presses Test Workflow, and
watches it run - the opposite of what happens in production.
Verified before fixing: trigger -> work (succeeds) -> cleanup on an 'error'
edge executed all three steps in the simulator.
rules: Two independent things decide this and they are not the same.
sourceOutput is which HANDLE the edge leaves from. A condition node draws
two, 'true' and 'false'; every other node has one unnamed output, which
means null or 'default'. A named branch is answered first: an edge on the
'false' handle must not run merely because the condition node did not throw.
An edge claiming a true/false branch whose source produced no verdict is an
error, because following it - or its sibling - would be a guess.
condition is what the EdgeConditionPanel writes. null and 'default' behave
as 'success'. 'error' follows only when the source failed. 'always' follows
either way, which is the point of a cleanup step. Anything else is an error:

Both apply. A 'true' branch edge whose condition is 'error' needs the verdict
